name: The Index IS the company — Michelin, inverted

kill.bet: "The Index IS the company — Michelin, inverted": stop treating the Cost Index as marketing for an unused SaaS and make it the business. Publish a stipulated, dollar-denominated "Muntin Reference Plate" as the quotable headline; fix four "rungs of citation capture" (number, definition, cadence, permanence via DOI); liquidate ~500 off-thesis pages; and sell three labour products over data that stays free forever — a $250-500/mo Reference Desk, $2,500-7,500 custom baskets, a $1,000-5,000/yr certified feed — so the first dollar needs no billing code, no Stripe SKU, no launch, and no correctness work on the food-cost identity.

fatalFlaws.attack: The proposal's load-bearing premise — "What the index is missing is not rigor, it is the four rungs of citation capture" — is false. The public machine-readable feed is publishing a BLS index value as a $393.06/lb wholesale price, right now, and the gate written to catch exactly that failure passes. Every one of the twelve moves amplifies this artifact: 164 embed cards, a DOI, a CC0 grant, a press kit inviting journalists to fetch it. This is the proposal violating its own stated sequencing principle — it opens a channel before the thing that channel inspects is correct.
fatalFlaws.evidence: `cost-index/feed.json` → ground-beef: {unit:"lb", basis:"wholesale", currency:"USD", reference:{date:"2026-06-01", priceUsd:393.06, source:"bls"}}. `cost-index/ground-beef/series.json` declares basis "wholesale" for the whole series while its last three live-captured (reconstructed:false) observations are 376.74 / 385.34 / 393.06 from source `bls`. `series.csv` correctly stamps those same rows `index` per-observation — the JSON strips it. Meanwhile `cost-index/index.json` prints $5.51/lb for the same slug at a different asOf: two published surfaces disagree by 71×. I ran `node scripts/check-cost-index-basis-leak.mjs` — it returns "✓ OK — every rendered $ traces to a dollar-basis level in the source", because it cross-references at the INGREDIENT level (ground-beef does have one $5.51 wholesale level) and never checks the basis of the specific observation rendered. The gate's own docstring names this exact failure ("a stored index … reads as '$4.03/lb' the instant a consumer treats it as a price") and cites the salmon-fillet precedent.

fatalFlaws.attack: The Reference Plate — the proposal's "rung one and the single highest-value move on the board" — cannot be built from this data, and the sentence that is supposed to make it honest ("a stipulation cannot be wrong, only more or less useful") is false. A pack weight is not a free stipulation; it is an unrecorded property of the source quote. Asserting one is inventing a number about the world, which is precisely what the fact gate exists to forbid.
fatalFlaws.evidence: Unit census of `cost-index/feed.json` (82 shipping ingredients): 65 carton, 12 lb, 4 sack, 1 dozen. `data/cost-index-sources.json#ingredients.tomato` declares eight AMS terminal markets with `unit:"carton"`, `reducer:"mostlyMid"`, and NO package weight or size/grade field anywhere — so $21.50 is a mid-reducer over heterogeneous carton specs, not a single package. No series.json carries a package descriptor. `tools/_shared/portion-bridge.js` UNIT_FAMILIES contains no carton, sack, or dozen; `_normalizeUnitToken` returns null and `unitsCompatible` returns false — so the proposal's stated build ("Σ via the parity-locked conversion") returns incompatible for 70 of 82 references. Five of the nine components the proposal names by dollar figure (russet-potato/sack, onion/sack, romaine/carton, tomato/carton, eggs/dozen) are exactly the unbridgeable ones. And this was already tried: `data/cost-plate-drift.json` prices archetype plates via `quoteAtPortion`, its `_doc` states "mis-scaled levels (>$60/lb) and non-bridgeable units are excluded and counted, never guessed", every surviving driver is a per-lb protein or butter, no produce appears in any archetype, and the file "ships to no page."

fatalFlaws.attack: The proposal's headline noun is a false license claim, and its constitutional clause is internally impossible. "Free, CC0" appears in the title, the positioning, the /press/ spec, the certified-feed product and the Day-90 signal — but the repo already decided the opposite, and the No Commercial Use clause is incompatible with both CC0 and CC BY. This lands on the one page whose entire job is to be trusted by a fact-checker on a two-hour deadline.
fatalFlaws.evidence: `cost-index/open-data-catalog.json`: "Rights split (ADR-015/ADR-017): raw US-government passthroughs are CC0 (public domain); Muntin's value-added compilations are CC BY 4.0" — counts {total:23, cc0:15, ccby:8}. A stipulated recipe × published references is unambiguously a Muntin compilation, so the plate is CC BY, not CC0. CC BY 4.0 expressly permits commercial use; CC0 waives all rights — you cannot bolt "no vendor may cite a reading in advertising" onto either and still name the license. `cost-index/menu-pricing/study/datacite.json` (the record the plan calls "one form away") carries rightsIdentifier `cc-by-4.0`. There is no LICENSE file in the storefront repo at all.

fatalFlaws.attack: The revenue model has a hard, low ceiling the proposal never computes: all three labour products are founder-hours-linear, and the plan budgets ~6h to SELL the Desk and zero hours to DELIVER it. Success is the failure mode. Worse, product (2) puts the very correctness debt the bet claims to remove from the critical path back onto it.
fatalFlaws.evidence: Product (1) is "a monthly written interpretive read plus a subscriber-named ingredient watchlist plus direct access to the analyst" — judgment and relationship, the two things the agent workforce explicitly cannot supply. At a conservative 4 h/client/month, 5 clients = 20 h/month, which consumes the entire 13-26 h/month budget and leaves nothing for the 45-min edition, the 90-day list, or Ledger. Ceiling ≈ 5 × $400 × 12 = $24k/yr gross at zero remaining capacity. Product (2), "a basket weighted to one group's actual purchase mix," requires ingesting that group's purchases — either the Purchases leg the proposal defers ("stay off the critical path to revenue, because nothing in the index touches them") or unbudgeted manual founder extraction. Product (3) sells an SLA and "a human who answers" from a company whose own daily refresh depends on keys on the founder's Mac (the plan's own item 2) and which has no measured uptime record to price against.

fatalFlaws.attack: Item 1 — the plan's own #1 priority, the move it says everything else depends on — is arithmetically wrong against the code it cites by line number. Widening the broadcast filter does NOT make 775 subscribers reachable; it reaches 90 and silently drops 685, then records the edition as delivered.
fatalFlaws.evidence: `src/worker.js` a few lines below the cited 8793: `const CAP = 90;   // Resend free tier is 100/day — stay under; larger lists need batching/queue.` and `if (sent >= CAP) { skipped++; continue; }`. The stamp-on-success block (lines ~8813-8815) then writes `cost-index:broadcast:<asOf>` with a 120-day TTL, and the handler's first act is `if (already) return {status:'already-sent'}` — so a same-edition re-fire to reach the remaining 685 returns already-sent. The plan scopes no batching, no queue, and no paid Resend tier. The claim "makes 775 existing subscribers reachable instead of 2" is false as written.

fatalFlaws.attack: "What We Stop" — roughly 500 distinct page deletions, the change the proposal calls "the single highest-leverage change to what a model believes Muntin is" — carries zero founder hours, zero agent sessions, and zero position in the 90-day list. It is the one thing this company has demonstrably never done, and the plan simultaneously adds gates under a one-in-one-out rule while naming none of the retirees.
fatalFlaws.evidence: `data/content-intent.json#summary`: deadWeight 162, byKeepVerdict {merge:60, freeze:36, retire:14}, byTopicCluster retired-web-SEO 200, thesis.allPages {servesThesis:832, neither:295, retiredLine:200}. Each deletion cascades through _redirects, sitemap, `data/link-graph.json`, `claims.json#used_in`, count sentinels, EN↔ES parity, hreflang orphans, the audio manifest and the idem registry — against 320 gates. Storefront CLAUDE.md records the one prior retirement (the /course/ subsystem, PR #530) as a campaign in which `check-idem-coverage` and `check-gate-coverage` failed until the registries caught up. The plan adds `check-reference-plate`, `check-src-sentinel` and a corrections check while declaring "Every new gate in this plan must name the one it replaces in the same commit" — and names none.

fatalFlaws.attack: Item 6 reverses a documented founder call while explicitly claiming it does not. The 2026-07-09 call is about AUTHORSHIP, not just publication, and the proposal retires exactly the thing the call preserved.
fatalFlaws.evidence: `.github/workflows/cost-index-dispatch.yml` header (named in CLAUDE.md as the source of truth): "the monthly dispatch is HAND-WRITTEN and hand-published each month; no cron generates or publishes posts … the machine reminds, humans write." The proposal's item 6: "machine-drafted and human-signed … Retires: hand-authoring the edition" and "without breaking the 2026-07-09 founder call that reserves publication to a human." The call reserves authorship, not merely the publish button.

fatalFlaws.attack: The /cost-index/track-record/ page — pitched as "the single most credible artifact either repo owns" — would permanently publish an undisclosed threshold redefinition, on the page whose entire job is to prove this company does not do that.
fatalFlaws.evidence: `cost-index/calibration.json`: nominal 0.80, pooledCoverage 0.767, minItemCoverage 0.731, underCovering 0. `scripts/build-cost-index-calibration-report.mjs:55`: `if (r.coverage < 0.70) underCovering++;` — under-covering is measured against 0.70, not against the 0.80 nominal the same object publishes. "0.767 coverage against 0.80 nominal with zero under-covering items," printed as a permanent citable claim, is a hostile statistician's first paragraph.

fatalFlaws.attack: The DOI mechanic is misdescribed and its side effect is irrevocable. Zenodo↔GitHub mints a DOI over a tagged release of a SOURCE REPOSITORY — it would permanently archive all 1,327 pages, including the 200-page retired-web-SEO cluster the same plan is deleting and any uncorrected edition, in a place nothing can retract. The prepared record also describes a different object under a different license.
fatalFlaws.evidence: `cost-index/menu-pricing/study/datacite.json`: resourceType "Working paper (practitioner field report; not peer-reviewed)", title "The Menu-Pricing Playbook", rights CC BY 4.0 — a working paper, not the index, not CC0. "Muntin is one form away" overstates the state of readiness for an index DOI. The correct instrument for a citable dataset is a Zenodo dataset deposit of the CC-licensed bulk archive, which the plan lists separately and does not connect.

fatalFlaws.attack: The Refusals line and the outreach line are both estimated with the same optimism that produced a 26% audit close rate. Under an absolute fact gate, an agent turning a one-sentence gap reason into reportage on USDA/NOAA data programs either fabricates (blocked) or restates the sentence. And ten substantive conversations with named signers, from zero prior outbound in fifteen months, is not a 6-hour activity.
fatalFlaws.evidence: `data/cost-index.json#coverage.gaps` is 42 one-sentence entries; the three the plan names as first installments are literally gaps[0..2] (leg-of-lamb, whole-branzino, oyster-mushroom). Turning "LMR feed is volume-only; cut prices are PDF-only" into publishable journalism requires original reporting on mandatory-reporting rules — founder-grade work, budgeted at "1 agent session … ~2h founder review per batch." Separately, the Day-45 kill signal requires all ten conversations complete, while outreach sits twelfth of twelve and two of the ten targets (trade-press desks) depend on /press/, which is item ten.

fatalFlaws.attack: A small evidence error that understates the freshness problem the plan is built to fix.
fatalFlaws.evidence: The plan says "Two frozen series are basket contributors." Cross-referencing `data/cost-index-health.json` asOf dates against `data/cost-basket-weights.json`: vegetable-oil (0.12, 67 days stale), shrimp (0.04, 67 days), salmon-fillet (0.03, 67 days) — at least three, carrying 19% of declared basket weight, all `directional` confidence. Also `withDollarLevel: 93` but feed ships 82, and `highEligible: 0` — no ingredient in the index reaches the top confidence tier, with 62 of 100 at `low`.

kill.survives: Four things survive a hostile reading, and they are not small. (1) The strategic reframe is correct and is the cheapest first-dollar path in the register: selling labour over free data genuinely removes billing.ts, the missing $19 SKU, `stripe_subscriptions.org_id`, the nonexistent /cockpit route and the 2026-11-13 GA date from the critical path, and 5 buyers at $400/mo beats 105 buyers at $228/yr for the same money — that arithmetic is real. (2) The 90-day plan's founder budget genuinely fits: summing its own estimates gives ~16 hours across the quarter, ~5.3 h/month against 13-26 available. (3) Item 4 is verified accurate to the character and addresses a live brand-threatening defect. (4) Item 2 correctly identifies the fetch-off-the-Mac move as the only one no agent can execute and the one protecting the only unfabricatable asset — and correctly reasons that a read-only government data key is not a real credential boundary. Unposting $19 and pulling GA off the calendar is correct and costs nothing. The "How It Fails" section is unusually honest: it pre-names the right failure (no institutional buyer), marks every price as an unvalidated hypothesis, and sets dated falsifiable kill signals. That is better epistemics than most of what this company has shipped.
kill.strongestPart: Item 4 — correct the July dispatch in place, repoint all 165 `<!-- src: -->` annotations at the frozen `data/cost-index-editions.json` snapshot, write `scripts/check-src-sentinel.mjs`, wire it into check-all, and ship an append-only `/cost-index/corrections/` whose every entry names the gate that now prevents recurrence. I verified every element: `grep -o "<!-- src:"` on `blog/cost-index-2026-07/index.html` returns exactly 165; `scripts/check-src-sentinel.mjs` does not exist on disk; the page contains exactly one "re-checked in CI" string, in a citation drawer that also prints "data/cost-revisions.json (append-only revision ledger, 2,080 entries)" against a live `count: 10294`. So the flagship post tells a stranger to verify claims against a CI gate that was never written, and the number it invites them to check is off by 5×. This is the only move on the board that makes the instrument MORE CORRECT rather than louder, it converts an unenforced prose convention into a machine-checked one, and its diagnosis — static prose annotated at live files, a parallel convention operating outside the fact gate — is exactly right and generalizes to every dated post on the site.
kill.repair: Invert the quarter: spend it making the instrument TRUE, not loud. Concretely — (a) Rewrite the basis gate to check the basis of each RENDERED OBSERVATION against its source key, not the ingredient's best available level; that single change catches $393.06/lb ground beef, and until it is green nothing is embedded, DOI'd, pressed or CC-licensed. Reconcile feed.json / index.json / series.json onto one asOf and one basis per slug. (b) Ship item 4 unchanged — it is already correct. (c) KILL the Reference Plate as specified. If a quotable dollar number is still wanted, restrict it to the ~12 references already denominated per pound with no conversion — call it a protein-and-dairy reference, not a plate, publish the per-lb list itself as the quotable object, and invent no pack weight for any carton or sack. If the plate is kept, the pack weight must be sourced from the AMS report's own package field and captured at fetch time in `data/cost-index-sources.json`, at which point it is a measurement and not a stipulation — that is a data-capture project, not a thirty-minute founder signature. (d) Replace every "CC0" in the positioning with the repo's actual ADR-015/017 split (gov passthroughs CC0, Muntin compilations CC BY 4.0), add a LICENSE file, and delete the No Commercial Use clause — or stop calling the result a Creative Commons license. (e) Fix the 90-send cap and the per-asOf stamp before widening the broadcast filter, or the first widened send burns the impression on 90 of 775 and marks the month done. (f) Move the ten conversations from twelfth to FIRST, weeks 1-3. They cost 6 hours, require no artifact that does not already exist, are the only move that tests the bet, and the proposal itself says so — then sequences them last, behind eleven items of building. If fewer than three produce a named signer, the entire storefront program is unnecessary and the quarter is saved. (g) Give "What We Stop" real hours and a position in the list, or cut it — an uncosted 500-page deletion in a company that has retired one subsystem in fifteen months is not a plan, it is a wish.

name: Sell to the bookkeeper; the restaurants come free

kill.bet: Sell to the bookkeeper; the restaurants come free. — Re-aim Muntin from a $19/location direct-to-owner tool to a firm-billed practice subscription ($150/mo + $30/seat + $39/client, ten-client minimum) sold to 8-10 DMV restaurant-specialist bookkeeping firms, on the argument that the accounting-firm product is already built and already correct; ship the AP→GL→post→workpaper leg on day one, withhold the food-cost identity behind six named defects, and publish the defect register as the flagship sales artifact.

fatalFlaws.attack: The day-one product does not exist. The bet's whole sequencing rests on 'what ships first, because it is already built and already correct: capture → GL-code → post → prove the period is closed → hand over a workpaper.' The posting path has never posted a real extracted invoice. It synthesizes its input from an HTTP request header and dry-runs by default.
fatalFlaws.evidence: apps/api/src/routes/integrations/posting.ts:166-168 — 'Build a minimal extraction stand-in so the resolver + the payload preview have data to operate on. The full extraction lookup wires when the Neon extractions-store ships; until then we synthesise a placeholder.' Line 178-199: the payload is read from the `x-muntin-extraction` request header; the fallback returns `vendor_canonical_name: "Unknown vendor"` and `line_items: []`. Line 408: '(Neon extractions-store lands)'. Line 634: `const dryRun = !flagOn || body.force_dry_run === true;` → returns `{status: "queued_dry_run", would_post: …}` behind `INTEGRATIONS_QBO_ENABLED`/`INTEGRATIONS_XERO_ENABLED` (line 160-161), with the comment at 216-219 'an operator must populate the vendor before flipping the env flag on.' The proposal audited these files by LINE COUNT (444/909/955/3665 — all of which I confirmed exact) and inferred function from size. The one check it never ran is whether the bytes execute against real data.

fatalFlaws.attack: The $39/client price is arithmetically unsellable, because the plan's own release rule withholds the only thing that justifies it. Gate the food-cost identity and the day-one firm product is document capture + GL posting — which is precisely Dext's job, at 2.2× the anchor the proposal itself cites, from a vendor with zero users and a published defect list.
fatalFlaws.evidence: $39 ÷ $17.70 (the proposal's own Dext anchor) = 2.20×. The stated differentiator is 'restaurant fluency, not cheapness' — which resolves to (a) the measured food-cost number, withheld by the plan's own §Correctness release rule pending six defect closures + a db-verify contract test + a CPA review, and (b) catch-weight handling, which IS defect #2 and is scheduled 'fix second,' i.e. unfixed when the first firm is pitched. So a firm is asked to pay 2.2× market for strictly less than market delivers. The plan lists 'the first firm that gets to pricing asks for a per-client rate under $20' as early-warning signal #3 — that is not a risk to monitor, it is the arithmetically correct valuation of what is actually on offer. And ARPU is $39, never $99: the $99 tier cannot be sold in the 90 days the plan covers, so the headline $540/firm and $52k ARR are the *only* attainable figures, not conservative ones.

fatalFlaws.attack: 'One login, every restaurant client, one review queue' is architecturally forbidden, and the prerequisite that would unforbid it appears nowhere in the 90-day plan. The cockpit is not 'one Next.js route away' — it is a per-request single-org switcher, and the promise sold is a cross-org aggregate read.
fatalFlaws.evidence: apps/api/src/routes/cockpit.ts is 145 lines. `GET /workspaces` returns `listForUser(auth.user_id)` mapped to `{org_id, role, last_used_at, current}` — no client names, no queue depths, no counts. `POST /switch` sets a `muntin_workspace` cookie whose own comment says it is 'NOT an authz grant: require-auth re-validates the membership via findActive on EVERY request' — i.e. every request resolves to exactly ONE org. Stores are RLS-first via `set_config('app.org_id',…,true)` (CLAUDE.md; confirmed across activity-store, catalog-store, charge-mapping-store, documents-store, cost-watch-scan). One Next.js route over that API renders a list of opaque org IDs and a switch button. The plan's own build-item 2 — a `firms` entity inverting `stripe_subscriptions.org_id` so the firm is the billing subject — is the actual prerequisite for the cockpit, the queues, the billing and the ten-client minimum alike. It appears in the First-90-Days list ZERO times: no session count, no founder hours, no migration number, no `db-verify` entry, no security ADR. The plan schedules 20 sales calls and a billing SKU in front of a foundation it never schedules at all.

fatalFlaws.attack: The correctness firewall the plan draws does not exist. It withholds 'the food-cost identity' and ships 'the AP leg' — but two of its own six named defects are AP defects. Withholding a percentage does not quarantine a missing credit memo or a mispriced catch-weight line, because both are wrong in the ledger the workpaper and the GL posting read.
fatalFlaws.evidence: apps/api/src/lib/verdicts-store.ts:1162-1169 filters `unit_price_cents > 0 && quantity > 0`, whose own comment says it 'drops credit memos / returns … and free-goods / zero-price promo lines.' apps/api/src/lib/queue.ts:1129-1132 writes `{sku, pack_size, description, quantity, unit_price_cents}` — no `line_total` field exists in the observation at all. A credit memo is an AP artifact; a CPA finds it in the first bank reconciliation, not in the food-cost tab. The plan's defence — 'the dropped lines still land in the Ledger + CSV via the extraction record' — is verdicts-store's own comment, not a verification that the roll-up, the signed IIF/CSV workpaper (accountant-handoffs.ts) and the posting payload read the extraction record rather than the observation layer. The plan asserts 'not one step of [capture → GL-code → post → workpaper] depends on Beginning + Purchases − Ending = Usage' — true and irrelevant; the defects are upstream of the split, in the shared line-item layer.

fatalFlaws.attack: The #1 storefront move is built on a page in the wrong repo, protected by a gate that does not govern it, and on five dated competitor facts that exist in neither repo and in no verified fact. This is the same class of inherited error as the repo-visibility one — except the plan proposes to PUBLISH it through an absolute fact gate.
fatalFlaws.evidence: `grep -rli hubdoc` across /home/user/potentially-profitable returns ZERO files. The page is Muntin-Invoice-Decoder/apps/web/app/(marketing)/switch/hubdoc/page.tsx — the PRIVATE product app, behind the domain the proposal itself calls one 'nobody reaches,' and not governed by the storefront's `check-fabrications.mjs` / sourced-claims.json apparatus. So 'a live liability on a site whose entire brand is a CI-enforced fact gate' is wrong on repo, wrong on gate, and wrong on exposure. I confirmed the proposal's own measurement — sourced-claims.json contains 0 occurrences of hubdoc, dext, marginedge, quickbooks — but the same grep kills the fix: the 2026-05-08 shutdown date, Dext $17.70, MarginEdge ~$350, R365 $469-499 and [me] finance's 2023-06-27 launch appear in NO verified fact and in NEITHER repo. Rewriting the page 'to past tense' registers an unsourced dated claim about a named company from a container with no primary-source access. Separately, the live lede already asserts 'Hubdoc reads with their OCR + a human-review queue offshore' in EN and ES — an unregistered factual claim about a named competitor's labour practices, which the plan preserves while fixing only the tense.

fatalFlaws.attack: Switching on EXTRACT_VENDOR_TRUST_ACTIVE does the opposite of what the plan claims. The gate is per-(org, vendor) and requires a MATURED profile — so it accelerates the Nth invoice from a vendor an org has already learned, and delivers exactly zero improvement to 'a firm's first ten uploads,' the one case the plan says it fixes.
fatalFlaws.evidence: services/extract/vendor_trust_gate.py header: the layout-template gates are 'replaced by the vendor-profile gates (synonym_only method, ACTIVE vendor profile, header-compat + role-map consistency)'; the predicate takes `org_id, vendor_id, observed_headers, observed_role_map, profile_store`. A new firm's client org has no profiles, so no clause can fire. The 24%→62% figure is measured by cli/vendor_trust_shadow.py on a 919-doc corpus that is ONE operator's already-matured 8-12 specialty vendors (constants.py:621-623). Compounded at the plan's own ceiling — 100 firms, ~1,200 restaurants, 8-12 specialty distributors each — the channel needs thousands of vendor profiles matured from zero, while templates are harvested in Python (engine_pkg/harvest.py) against a store apps/api cannot reach (templates-store.ts, 184 lines, a stub). The 'specialty long tail no incumbent will template' is booked as a moat; it is a per-client onboarding cost that scales linearly with the only revenue line.

fatalFlaws.attack: The kill criterion is engineered to misfire, by the plan's own mechanism. §How It Fails states firms do not change AP tooling mid-engagement and that the switching moment is January — then sets the falsification date at 2026-11-07 and requires a signed pilot by then.
fatalFlaws.evidence: Proposal §How It Fails: 'firms do not change AP tooling mid-engagement. The real switching moment is January… A bet started in August has one shot in January and then waits twelve months.' Proposal §kill criterion: 'if by 2026-11-07 (ninety days) fewer than three firms have taken a call AND fewer than one has agreed to run a single client through a pilot, the bet is falsified.' Under the author's own model, a November reading of pilot conversion carries no information — the population is structurally unable to convert until January. The criterion therefore either fires a false negative on a live bet, or gets argued away in exactly the manner the sentence 'stated in advance so it cannot be argued away later' was written to prevent. This is the one discipline the plan offers and it is self-cancelling.

fatalFlaws.attack: Capacity is understated by omitting the founder's standing obligations, ~328 human freeze/retire judgments the plan itself creates, and an employer-data authorization the certification mechanism silently requires. And the plan is a 13-item list, in a company where zero closures have ever come from working a list.
fatalFlaws.evidence: Explicit founder lines total ~25.5h/90d (1h ADR + 0.5h build-ingredient-state-record + ~15h calls + ~1h price call + ~0.5h role call + ~0.5h location call + 6h month E2E + 1h CPA) against 39-78h available — fine on paper. Unbooked: three hand-written monthly Cost Index editions (the founder writes them; check-cost-index-dispatch-fresh reds at 38 days); ~328 per-page retire/freeze judgments (96 glossary + ~36 sheets + 52 cluster + 162 dead) where check-positioning-drift 'deliberately does not auto-classify; it only guarantees the judgement is made' — that judgement is human and per-page; and review of ~20 agent sessions by the only reviewer, in a company where the contract loaded in 1 of 108 transcripts. The plan also names the archive decay (26 of 100 series frozen 58-77d against a 120-day drop cliff, the unfabricatable 2,025 live-captured points) as a consequence and then allocates it nothing — a disclosed, unmitigated loss of the one asset the verified facts call unfabricatable. Separately, certification mechanism (b) — 'one full month end-to-end on Tacombi's own invoices and counts… reviewed by a working restaurant CPA' — escalates from 7 committed fixtures to a full month of an employer's AP and inventory, processed through a product the founder intends to sell and disclosed to an outside CPA. Don is an FOH manager, not the owner; no artifact in either repo establishes authorization. The linchpin of the release rule is the one step carrying real legal exposure, and it gets one line and six hours. Base rate: 13 workstreams × a 26% close rate ≈ 3.4, and the causal record is worse — zero closures have ever come from working an audit's list.

kill.survives: A great deal, and the diagnosis is better than the plan. The core observation is true and I verified every load-bearing count: apps/web/app/(product)/bookkeeper/ is exactly 20 files; bookkeeper.ts 444, accountant-handoffs.ts 909, statement-reconciliations.ts 432, gl-rules.ts 357, charge-mappings.ts 276; integrations 3,665 across QBO 668 / Xero 629 / posting 955 / bulk-post 484; stripe-tiers.ts accountant = basePriceCents 15000, seatPriceCents 3000, maxSeats 50, hasCockpit true; pricing-constants.ts:48-49 accountant and accountantSeat are BOTH billable:true, and priceIdForTier has a real STRIPE_PRICE_ACCOUNTANT_BASE branch that the $19 founding rate does not. billing.ts:175 sets line_items[0][quantity] to seats exactly as claimed. cockpit.ts and the index.ts wiring exist.
