lens: The one-person reality critic — founder-hours arithmetic and the agent-review bottleneck
thesis: All six proposals are written for a founder who does not exist, and the proof is in the last seven days: between 2026-07-31 and today, the product repo received zero human-initiated commits and the storefront received three bot data refreshes and nothing else — the only August activity in either repo is this audit. Every plan is a 90-day plan denominated in a July (340 storefront commits, 148 product) that has already stopped happening. The harder finding is that the review bottleneck was not crossed recently; it was crossed no later than June and every headline defect in the verified-facts list is its downstream symptom. In July the product repo alone took 26,526 net insertions of hand-written TypeScript/Python/SQL across 241 files; at a generous 300 reviewed lines per hour that is ~88 hours of reading against a total discretionary budget of 13-26 hours a month — a 3.5-7x overrun from one of two repos. The founder's observed behavior confirms it: he merged 101 PRs since June 1, with 19 of 68 product merges landing under 15 minutes after the previous one and a 12-minute median same-session gap. An empty `if (estimated) {}`, a purchases store whose own header documents its missing location predicate, `hasCockpit: true` sold against a route that does not exist, and 56 tautological gates are not bugs that survived review — they are bugs that were never read, and "prior audits close at 26% with zero closures ever from working a list" is the same arithmetic measured from the other end. The single cleanest grader on the board sits in the storefront right now: `data/cost-index.json` is two days old because a bot writes it, and `data/cost-index-editions.json` is thirty-two days stale because a human signs it — same company, same month, machine rituals hold and human rituals lapse. Not one of the six documents assigns a single founder-hour to reviewing the 11-20 agent sessions it commissions, which understates every plan's true personal cost by 4-7 hours at his demonstrated rubber-stamp rate and by 26-80 hours at honest review. The correct read is therefore inverted from what all six assume: agent output is not the scarce resource being spent, it is the load being generated, and any bet that increases it makes the company measurably worse.

rulings.subject: dream-vindication-instrument (the Market Sheet)
rulings.why: SMALLEST PERSONAL FOOTPRINT ON THE BOARD. Its own founder lines sum to ~10.5h/90d (1h retraction language + 1h Mac fetch + 1h layout approval + 2h rep experiment + 0.5h send copy + 1h retirement call + 2h pricing + 2h frozen-series decision); add ~4h of uncounted review across its ~12 agent sessions at his demonstrated 20-min-per-session rate and the true cost is ~14.5h — the only bet that fits inside a realistic 23-62h quarterly discretionary window with margin. The decisive reason is not the total but the SHAPE of the validating experiment: Don hands a printed sheet to a distributor rep in weeks 3-4. No scheduling, no strangers, no travel, no calendar collision — the rep comes to Tacombi during a shift he is already working. Every other bet's validating experiment requires him to originate contact with people who do not know him (15h of cold calls in bet 1, 6-10h of outreach in bets 2 and 3, 3h of CPA conversations plus a 6h month in bet 4). This is the only proposal whose central unknown can be falsified as a by-product of employment he already has. CONDITIONS, both structural: (1) INVERT THE ORDER. As written, 2-3 agent sessions build /market-sheet/ before the 2h rep test. Run the test first with a hand-made sheet — the bet then costs 2 founder-hours to falsify instead of 3 agent sessions plus 2 hours. (2) The rep-as-channel claim is the one assertion in the document with nothing behind it and it is structurally adverse: the rep works for the vendor the sheet is designed to argue against, so proposing him as unpaid distribution asks the adversary to carry the weapon. The document's own failure section anticipates the deflection ('that's not your landed cost') but never confronts that the channel and the opponent are the same person. Do not build distribution on it until the 2h test produces a verbatim quote.

rulings.subject: dream-index-is-the-company (Reference Plate + Reference Desk)
rulings.why: ~18 founder-hours by its own lines (1h unblock review + 1h key minting + 2h frozen-series triage + 0.5h correction call + 0.5h plate signature + 2.25h across three monthly edition signatures + 0.33h DOI + 0.33h press + ~4h Refusals review + 6h outreach), plus ~5h uncounted review across ~15 agent sessions = ~23h/quarter. Fits at the optimistic end. It contains the single best STRUCTURAL move on the entire board, and it is worth naming precisely because it is the correct answer to the bottleneck rather than a way around it: the Reference Plate converts a recurring founder judgment into a frozen, versioned artifact that a machine re-applies forever — 30 minutes once, then never again. 'Move the price fetch off the founder's Mac onto a scheduled runner' is the only line item in all six documents with NEGATIVE founder hours; it retires an obligation instead of adding one. CONDITIONS: (1) CUT the 10 outreach conversations (6h) from the 90 days. They test a price hypothesis the document itself marks as unvalidated, and nothing downstream is blocked on the answer; that 6h is better spent not being spent. (2) The recurring 45-minute monthly edition signature is the load-bearing assumption and it is ALREADY FAILING — `data/cost-index-editions.json` was last touched 2026-07-06, thirty-two days ago, while the bot-written `data/cost-index.json` is two days old. The bet makes a human ritual the spine of the company on the same week that exact ritual lapsed. Do not proceed past the plate until one edition has actually shipped on schedule.

rulings.subject: dream-open-institution (record layer + attestation)
rulings.why: ~15 founder-hours by its own lines (0.25h wording + 2min curl + ~1h Mac session + 1.5h secrets/security call + 0.5h monetization ADR + 1h first attestation template + 10h twenty conversations + 0.5h freeze-vs-delete), plus ~4.7h across ~14 sessions = ~20h. The record layer specifically is the highest agent-leverage, lowest-founder-cost work anywhere on this board: five surfaces (/corrections/, /calibration/, /refusals/, /freshness/, /decisions/) generated from JSON already sitting on disk, regenerating on deploy, structurally incapable of lapsing, requiring approximately zero founder judgment because they render measured data rather than prose. That is exactly the right shape for a company whose human review capacity is exhausted. CONDITIONS: (1) SHIP THE RECORD LAYER, DEFER ATTESTATION. The document admits its own trap — 'the first fifty will be hand-signed and hand-explained' — which converts revenue directly into founder-hours in a company that has none. Build the certificate generator only after someone asks for one; the 10h of conversations is the wrong instrument to find that person. (2) It proposes ADDING `check-trust-cadence.mjs` to a system already carrying 320 checks of which 56 are tautologies. Its justification (the gate retires founder-hours) is the only acceptable one, so it passes on that reasoning alone — but it must land with a named retirement in the same commit or it becomes the 321st thing nobody reads.

rulings.subject: dream-price-inversion ($600/location signed monthly close)
rulings.why: FAILS ON ITS OWN ARITHMETIC, STATED IN ITS OWN TEXT. Setup is ~16.5h (0.5h price call + 1h ADR + 1h location attribution + 6h real month + 1h shadow report + 2h specimen note + 3h CPA conversations + 1h price + 1h retirement sign-off) plus ~4.7h review = ~21h, which is survivable. The recurring cost is not: the document itself states '~20 founder-minutes of close review per location per month, 40 locations is 13.3 hours/month against 13-26 available.' That is 51-100% of TOTAL discretionary capacity consumed forever at the terminal state, and the 20-minute figure is invented — the document concedes `desk_minutes_per_close` is the number that decides everything and is unmeasured. This is the only bet that converts every dollar of revenue into a linearly-scaling founder obligation, which means it is capacity-dead at its own stated ceiling of $288K before it reaches it. Two further costs nobody priced: (a) a signed close is a professional judgment on a number produced by an engine the founder has never once run end to end, and the review he cannot give agent PRs is exactly the review a signature demands; (b) it asks a man employed full-time by one restaurant brand to sign monthly financial statements for forty others — an exposure question that appears nowhere in the document. The bet is a services business wearing software pricing, and the service is delivered by the one resource measured at 13-26 hours.

rulings.subject: dream-bookkeeper-platform (sell to accounting firms)
rulings.why: HIGHEST PERSONAL COST, WORST DOWNSIDE SHAPE. Founder lines sum to ~26h/90d — 1h ADR + 0.5h Mac + 0.5h role-permission + 15h calling twenty firms + 0.5h location attribution + 1h price call + 6h real month + 1h paid CPA + 0.5h retirement calls — the single largest founder line on the board, and it commissions ~18-20 agent sessions, adding ~6.3h of uncounted review for a true cost near 32h. Against 39-78h of quarterly capacity already carrying 159 quarter-hours of obligation at a measured 10% payment rate, this does not fit. To its credit, the schedule-collision objection does NOT hold — his commit hours show real 10:00-15:00 activity in both repos, so business-hours calls are physically possible; the constraint is pure volume, not clock. But the disqualifying feature is the downside: one firm relationship carries 12-25 restaurants, so a wrong number costs a book rather than a customer, and the wrongness is guaranteed by the same bottleneck that produced the defects it proposes to fix. The document's kill criterion (three firms take a call by day 90) does not test the market — it tests whether the founder made the calls, which after fifteen months and zero recorded outbound conversations is the least-supported assumption in the plan. It also front-loads 15h of cold outreach BEFORE the correctness work that would make the conversation survivable.

rulings.subject: dream-radical-narrowing (amputate to ~120 pages)
rulings.why: CORRECT DIAGNOSIS, LETHAL DOSE — and the most dangerous of the six. It is the only bet that attacks the bottleneck itself rather than routing around it, and that instinct is right. But its stated ~23h/90d (0.5h analytics + 1h amputation review + 0.5h yield fold + 3h correction wording + 2h re-headline naming + 1h send + 2h count-deletion decision + 1h billing + 4h invoice walk + 2h gate retirement + 2h/mo writing) omits the only cost that matters: reviewing ~15 agent sessions that irreversibly delete ~1,100 routes. Deletion is the ONE agent output class where founder review is both mandatory and non-compressible — you cannot batch-approve 1,100 removals the way he demonstrably batch-approves PRs at a 12-minute median gap with 19 of 68 landing under 15 minutes apart. At 300 reviewed lines/hour and 10h/month of review he can sustainably read ~3,000 lines; this amputation is orders of magnitude past that, so it WILL be merged unread, and unread deletion is the single error class with no recovery path. Its own document names 'the cut half-lands' as the modal outcome given a 26% historical closure rate; I agree and can now price it. THE SURVIVOR: its move 2 — the 162 measured dead-weight pages, the 78 orphan event pages, the 20 /open/ surfaces and the 103 pages at retiredLineScore ≥3, ~260 routes needing no traffic evidence — is genuinely safe, costs ~1 founder-hour of review, and establishes for the first time that this company can retire something. Do that subset and stop. The other 840 deletions are the failure.

rulings.subject: CROSS-CUTTING: the review bottleneck was crossed in June, not in the future
rulings.why: Every one of the six asks 'what should we build' when the measured constraint is 'what can be read.' July product-repo output was 26,526 net insertions of hand-written TS/TSX/PY/SQL across 241 files; at 300 reviewed lines/hour (an industry rule-of-thumb I am asserting, not measuring here — careful review runs 200-400 lines/hour) that is ~88 hours against 13-26 available, from ONE of two repos. Storefront July: 340 commits, 42 merges, median 23 files each, p90 1,359 files. Across both repos 47 distinct agent branches merged since June 1 (~20 sessions/month landing). THE THRESHOLD: at 10 hours/month spent reviewing, sustainable output is ~3,000 reviewed lines/month — roughly 11% of what the product repo alone shipped in July, and every bet on this board plans MORE than July. The crossing point is not ahead of the company; it is ~9x behind it. This reframes the audit's own headline fact: 'prior audits close at 26% and zero closures ever came from working an audit's list' is not a discipline failure, it is arithmetic — he cannot work a list because he cannot read the output of the sessions that would work it. The correct decision rule for all six proposals is therefore inverted: prefer the bet that generates the FEWEST reviewable artifacts per unit of validated learning, which is why the 2-hour rep test beats every 15-session build on this board.

rulings.subject: CROSS-CUTTING: not one document prices agent-session review time
rulings.why: THE LARGEST ACCOUNTING ERROR ACROSS ALL SIX. Every line reading '[Agent, 2 sessions]' or '[1 agent session. Founder: zero.]' is quoted at a founder cost of zero. That is false in both directions. At his DEMONSTRATED behavior (12-minute median same-session merge gap, 19 of 68 product merges under 15 minutes after the previous), ~20 minutes per session, the uncounted cost is 3.7h (bet 6, ~11 sessions) to 6.3h (bet 1, ~19 sessions) — enough to push bet 1 from 26h to 32h and past the fit line. At HONEST review of a median 13-23 file diff at 300 lines/hour, it is 2-4 hours per session, or 26-80 hours per bet — 1.5-4x each plan's entire stated founder budget. So every proposal here is either understated by ~25% (if he keeps rubber-stamping, which reproduces the defects) or understated by 300% (if he starts reading, which means none of them fit). There is no third branch. Any plan adopted from this board must add a line: 'founder review, N sessions × 20 min' — and if that line breaks the budget, the plan commissions fewer sessions rather than pretending the review is free.

rulings.subject: CROSS-CUTTING: machine rituals hold, human rituals lapse — grade every bet on this axis
rulings.why: The cleanest empirical grader available and it sits in the storefront right now: `data/cost-index.json` last written 2026-08-05 (two days, bot-authored) against `data/cost-index-editions.json` last written 2026-07-06 (thirty-two days, human-signed) — same repo, same month, same company. Corroborated across the board: the bots committed on 08-03 and 08-05 while the founder committed nothing to either repo between 07-31 and today, and the audit's own list of lapsed human obligations (warrant canary 89 days, transparency report 37 days, dispatch missed 2026-08-04) contains no machine-owned entry. THE RULE THIS YIELDS: any proposal whose revenue depends on a recurring human ritual is betting against the only measured behavioral regularity this company has. Applied — bet 4 fails hardest (a monthly signature per customer, scaling with revenue); bet 3's attestation fails (fifty hand-signed certificates); bet 1 fails (firm relationships are recurring human contact); bet 2 is exposed at exactly one point (the 45-min monthly edition signature, on the ritual that just lapsed); bet 6 is cleanest (the sheet regenerates from frozen editions; the founder approves one layout once). The corollary is the design principle every adopted plan should carry: convert each founder judgment into a frozen artifact a machine re-applies — which is precisely what bet 2's Reference Plate does, and it is the single best structural idea on this board regardless of which bet is chosen.

rulings.subject: CROSS-CUTTING: the intersection of all six is ~3 founder-hours and it is the actual decision
rulings.why: All six documents independently name the same four or five unblocking moves, and their combined founder cost is trivial: widen the broadcast filter at `src/worker.js:8793` (agent, ~0h founder — makes 775 collected subscribers reachable instead of 2); green the deploy, which currently exits 1 at 312 of 320 (~1h on his Mac for `build-ingredient-state-record`, the one item no container can clear); correct the 72 published falsehoods on `blog/cost-index-2026-07/` and ship `check-src-sentinel.mjs` (~0.5-1h of wording approval); move the FRED/BLS/AMS fetch onto a scheduled runner (~1h, one security call — and it is the only line in all six documents with negative recurring founder hours); name `no-llm-ci.sh` on the pages that already make the claim it proves (agent, 0h). That is ~3 founder-hours total for the moves that six independent strategies all agreed were prerequisites. Against a board where the cheapest full bet costs ~14.5h and the dearest ~32h, the honest recommendation is: pay the 3-hour intersection this month, run bet 6's 2-hour rep test alongside it, and defer the union until one of those two produces evidence. Six 90-day plans written for a founder who committed nothing in the last seven days should not be chosen between; they should be intersected.

lens: The honesty fence — where each bet would require Muntin to say something it cannot prove
thesis: The fence is thinner than the company believes: check-fabrications.mjs is a blocklist of five 2026-era patterns, sourced-claims.json holds 47 entries, and the "absolute fact gate" is otherwise a policy in a CLAUDE.md that loaded in 1 of 108 transcripts — so every bet that raises published-claim volume raises exposure faster than enforcement. Against that, four of six proposals headline the same sentence, "zero under-covering items," which is an artifact of build-cost-index-calibration-report.mjs:55 counting only items below 0.70 while nominal is 0.80, pooled realized is 0.767 and the worst item is 0.731 — and the July flagship already published the stricter version ("it under-covers by 2.8 points"), so these plans would regress the company's own standard on the very page meant to prove it does not overstate. Two bets fail on standing rather than fact: open-institution sells "certified" attestations that relyers would name in contracts with escalators, and the moment a reading settles money between two parties the sentence "no market participant submits a price to us" stops being adequate governance — Muntin has no oversight, no E&O, one person, and 10,294 revisions proving its published numbers move. Price-inversion fails three ways: an agent-run exception desk would have a language model read customer invoices, falsifying in substance the claim on 81 pages while no-llm-ci.sh stays green (a gate certifying a false claim is worse than no gate); the specimen close publishes Tacombi's complete September including vendor prices, which an FOH manager cannot consent to release; and "signed close," "certified," and a valuation_method stamped wac that is FIFO are accounting terms of art from a non-CPA. Vindication fails because fair-price-gap.js already states in Muntin's own code that a price above the wholesale reference is not proof of overpaying and refuses a verdict below a 60% gap — yet the Market Sheet exists to be laid on a table in exactly that argument, and it would print the flattering calibration half onto a permanent object that can never be corrected. The three survivors are conditional on narrow, mechanical fixes: the Reference Plate must never be spoken as a price level (the frozen-weights file forbids "never a national price level" and the plate mixes Atlanta cartons, Baltimore sacks and national pounds through stipulated pack weights); the Lock List must carry realized coverage beside every "commit," because it upgrades a next-week conformal band into a monthly assurance while the site's own editor's-note gate bans "next week's price" as a forecast; and the bookkeeper bet must forecloseat its delivered-price second-order thesis in writing rather than defer it, because a per-vendor ledger harvested from customers is a submitter lane with a laundered label — check-cost-index-independence.mjs already mechanically forbids the index pipeline reading any path containing invoice, customer, ledger or delivered-. No proposal fabricates headcount; all six name the one-person constraint and label their prices as unvalidated hypotheses, which is the one hard line every one of them respects.

rulings.subject: dream-index-is-the-company — the Reference Plate as the quotable headline
rulings.why: The plate sums Σ(qty × published reference) across incommensurable bases — acorn squash is an Atlanta carton, onion a Baltimore sack, ribeye a national LMR pound — converted through stipulated pack weights. The dream is right that a stipulation cannot be wrong, but the sentence it wants printed ("the wholesale ingredients for Muntin's reference plate cost $X.XX in August") is a PRICE LEVEL claim, and data/cost-basket-weights.json explicitly forecloses that: the index claims "a BASIS-AGNOSTIC RATE-OF-CHANGE for THIS declared basket — never a national price level, never 'what restaurants pay'." cost-index/feed.json's own disclaimer repeats it: "Not a delivered or retail price." CONDITIONS: (1) the plate total never appears without its basis disclosure on the same line; (2) it is never described as what ingredients, a restaurant, or anyone "costs" — only as the stipulated sum of named references on a date; (3) withholding-inheritance is built before first publication, not after. Everything else here clears the fence: correct-in-place before amplifying, /corrections/, /cost-index/freshness/, no forecast, no 101st ingredient, and the absolute no-submitters clause.

rulings.subject: dream-index-is-the-company — the Reference Desk's subscriber-named watchlist
rulings.why: The methodology page forecloses placement AND influence. A paid subscriber naming which ingredients get attention, plus "standing to put a question into the next edition," is a payer steering editorial attention — soft influence, but influence, and the independence sentence currently carries no caveat that would survive a hostile read of it. CONDITION: write the rule into the constitutional ADR that a paid watchlist changes what the analyst WRITES FOR THE SUBSCRIBER and never what the index publishes, measures, covers or prioritizes — and say so on the same page that sells the Desk, not only in the ADR.

rulings.subject: dream-open-institution — the attestation lane ("certified as-of statement," $250/cert)
rulings.why: This is the bet's revenue mechanism and it sells standing Muntin does not have. "Attestation" and "certified" are terms of art implying a licensed practitioner and an assurance framework; Muntin is one non-CPA. Worse, the stated use case — a group naming the index in a produce contract with an escalator, a landlord with percentage rent, a lawyer in a dispute — makes readings settle money between parties. That is precisely the incentive structure the independence sentence exists to preclude, and "no market participant submits a price to us" is an INPUT control, not governance: it says nothing about oversight, appeal, restatement policy, or conflicts once money rides on a print. Muntin would be certifying the durability of a series with a 10,294-entry revisions ledger, 0.767 realized band coverage against 0.80 nominal, and 18–26 series frozen 58–77 days. The record layer in this same document (/corrections/, /calibration/, /refusals/, /freshness/, /decisions/) is the strongest fence-compatible content in the entire register and should be salvaged into whichever bet wins — but the money mechanism, which is the bet, fails.

rulings.subject: dream-open-institution — "zero items under-covered their own stated band"
rulings.why: Verbatim proposed headline for /cost-index/calibration/. The stated band is 80%; realized pooled coverage is 0.767 and the worst item is 0.731. underCovering counts only items below 0.70 (build-cost-index-calibration-report.mjs:55) — a threshold that is nowhere published. blog/cost-index-2026-07 already printed the honest version: "it under-covers by 2.8 points… 2 items under-covering." Shipping the flattering half on the page whose entire job is proving Muntin does not overstate would be the single most self-refuting artifact the company could publish.

rulings.subject: dream-open-institution / dream-radical-narrowing — "a real Tacombi address … in a public MIT repo"
rulings.why: Factually false as written: Muntin-Invoice-Decoder is PRIVATE (verified via GitHub API 2026-08-07). The fixtures are a hygiene and employer-confidentiality problem, not a live public exposure. Both plans build urgency on this framing, and open-institution sequences a public redaction narrative around it — publishing "we closed a public exposure" would itself be a published falsehood. Redact the fixtures anyway (Don is an employee, and the data is Tacombi's), but never describe it publicly as a public exposure.

rulings.subject: dream-bookkeeper-platform — the delivered-price second-order thesis
rulings.why: "A firm that standardizes on Muntin generates a normalized, per-vendor, per-region ledger across its whole book … built from customers rather than from submitters, and therefore without touching the no-submitters clause." The methodology sentence does not make that distinction: it says no MARKET PARTICIPANT submits a price. A restaurant is a market participant; a bookkeeper acting for one is its agent. check-cost-index-independence.mjs enforces this mechanically — the number-producing pipeline may not read any path containing ledger, invoice, customer, waitlist, founding or delivered-. And the leak is already pre-authorized elsewhere: cost-basket-weights.json says the weights stand "pending Muntin's own aggregate buy data." "Not in year one" is not a foreclosure. Close it in the ADR with the peer-pool enhancement named in fair-price-gap.js, or the strongest sentence on the site acquires a caveat the day the first firm signs.

rulings.subject: dream-bookkeeper-platform — the competitor-fact content lane (Hubdoc, Dext, MarginEdge, Xero, R365)
rulings.why: sourced-claims.json contains 47 claims total and 4 mentions of those names combined; this plan needs dozens — a shutdown date, three price points, "12,000+ firms," a 2023-06-27 launch. Every one is a third-party fact that rots, on a site whose brand is that its facts do not. The proof is already live: /switch/hubdoc/ describes a product Xero killed on 2026-05-08 in the present tense, in EN and ES, and tells readers to log into it. CONDITIONS: (1) every competitor fact enters sourced-claims.json with source_url, date_verified and a named re-verification cadence before it reaches a page; (2) a gate reds when a competitor claim's date_verified ages past that cadence — this is the one new gate that earns its seat, because the lane cannot be maintained by memory. /for/bookkeepers/known-limits/ is the best fence-positive idea in the entire register: every line traces to a file and a line number, so it is unfalsifiable by construction, and it makes withholding the food-cost percentage legible rather than evasive.

rulings.subject: dream-price-inversion — the agent-run exception desk
rulings.why: 81 pages say "your data, no language model"; others say "no language model ever reads the invoices you hand the product" and "no language model touches the document." The desk's job is the 13–16% that does not reconcile — an agent session must OPEN the customer's invoice to author the template. The "rules, never numbers" protocol constrains the desk's OUTPUT; the published claim is about the READ. no-llm-ci.sh would stay green throughout, because it scans source imports and HTTP destinations, not who looked at a PDF — so the company's most falsifiable claim would be mechanically certified while being false in the world. That is strictly worse than having no gate, and it is the one asset this company cannot rebuild once spent.

rulings.subject: dream-price-inversion — /close/specimen/2026-09/, Tacombi's full month published
rulings.why: "One real month, in full, forever": four legs, dollar coverage, every exception receipt, every line, signed by Don. That is an employer's confidential purchasing data — vendor mix, negotiated unit prices, food cost — published permanently by a full-time FOH manager who is not the owner and cannot grant the consent. It is the unredacted-fixture problem deliberately scaled up and made the centerpiece. Not a fact-gate failure; a consent failure, which is the harder one. A synthetic or founder-owned specimen would carry the same demonstrative value; a real employer's month cannot be published at all.

rulings.subject: dream-price-inversion — selling a "signed close" at $600 as an accounting deliverable
rulings.why: "The way an audit firm sells an opinion," "a signed statement," "certified" — terms of art from a non-CPA, for a number a client puts in its books, with the Cost-Index market prior as a valuation basis ASC 330 does not permit and a valuation_method field stamped 'wac' for what is FIFO. The plan names all of this honestly and gates the price behind seven fixes, which is the one thing it gets right — but the deliverable's NAME makes a standing claim that no amount of correctness work confers. Sell an analysis, never an opinion.

rulings.subject: dream-radical-narrowing — the Lock List as the public headline
rulings.why: The most fence-native number in the register: derived deterministically in data/cost-lockfloat.json (lock 37, cushion 19, float 7, withhold 37, asOf 2026-08-04), CI-checked, hand-edit-nothing, a COUNT not a percentage of a construct, and documented in its own file as "a RISK read, never a direction or opportunity call." But the proposed prose — "priceable enough to commit to this month" — upgrades a next-week conformal interval into a monthly assurance to act, over bands realizing 76.7% against an 80% promise, and check-cost-index-editors-note.mjs bans the phrase "next week's price" as a forecast on the very same publication. CONDITIONS: (1) every Lock renders with the band's realized coverage, not its nominal; (2) the horizon is stated in the headline sentence (next-week band), not buried in methodology; (3) /cost-index/track-record/ prints "pooled coverage under-covers nominal by 3.3 points; worst item 0.731" BEFORE it prints the zero-under-covering count, or omits that count entirely.

rulings.subject: dream-radical-narrowing — deleting the food-cost identity rather than shipping it biased
rulings.why: The most fence-correct product decision anywhere in the register. The headline number is biased low three independent ways and location-contaminated; fixing it needs a CPA, a real month and founder hours that do not exist. Returning line_item_observations to the job it was built for, and shipping only per-line claims the operator can check against the paper in his hand, is the only version of this product where every printed claim is verifiable by its reader. It also removes the count, which is the $100–150/month of floor labor no price cut ever touched.

rulings.subject: dream-vindication-instrument — the Market Sheet as an argument-winning object
rulings.why: tools/_shared/fair-price-gap.js states, in Muntin's own committed code, that "a price sitting above the reference is NOT proof of overpaying — saying so would mislead," and refuses any verdict below a 60% gap because "a definitive overpayment finding needs the operator's true delivered price." The sheet is engineered to be carried into precisely that conversation to produce "standing." Careful sheet-face wording does not change what the object is FOR: the company would be manufacturing an implication it has already written down that it cannot support, and the rep's rebuttal is Muntin's own published position. The dream names this as its most likely failure and ships it anyway.

rulings.subject: dream-vindication-instrument — printing calibration and the $1,300 materiality figure on a permanent object
rulings.why: Two compounding problems. First, it prints "0.767 against 0.80 nominal … zero under-covering" on paper — the flattering-half framing, on an artifact that can never be recalled or corrected, which is the exact inverse of the corrections-ledger asset it is meant to embody. Second, it justifies $79/location by citing cost-watch-impact.ts's $25/week materiality floor as "= $1,300/yr = 1.37x the annual list." That floor is the minimum size of a price MOVE worth surfacing, not money found or saved; printing it as the value case is a savings claim with nothing behind it and collides head-on with fair-price-gap's refusal. Salvageable from this bet: check-sheet-provenance.mjs (frozen editions only, never a live file) is the single best gate proposed anywhere in the register, /no-llm/ and /corrections/ are right, the pack-shrink and vendor-ask engines are already honesty-gated and withhold correctly, and "stop writing rules into CLAUDE.md" is the truest sentence in all six documents.

rulings.subject: dream-vindication-instrument — retiring the dispatch cadence gate while 83 pages still promise the email
rulings.why: Deleting check-cost-index-dispatch-fresh.mjs from check-all retires the ALARM, not the PROMISE. 83 pages say a monthly edition is coming; src/worker.js:8793 already means 775 of 777 signups never receive one. Removing the gate leaves a published promise false and unmonitored — the precise shape of the 72 falsehoods, repeated deliberately. If the cadence is being retired, the 83 pages come down in the same commit, or the promise is restated as the event-triggered watch on those pages first.

rulings.subject: CROSS-CUTTING — "zero under-covering items" is the register's shared overclaim
rulings.why: Proposed as a flagship credibility headline in index-is-the-company, open-institution, radical-narrowing and vindication. Nominal 0.80, pooled realized 0.767, min item 0.731, and underCovering counts only items below an unpublished 0.70 floor. The honest sentence — already published once, in July — is: "We aim for 80% coverage. We measured 76.7% across 79,086 steps. The worst item ran 73.1%. No item fell below 70%." Any surface that prints the fourth sentence without the first three fails, and a fence-holding company should add the 0.70 threshold to the published methodology so the number can never again be quoted alone.

rulings.subject: CROSS-CUTTING — mass retirement vs the public /claims.json
rulings.why: sourced-claims.json carries 149 used_in edges (54 into es/, plus library, learn, tools and blog slugs), and build-claims-json.mjs copies them verbatim into a public, crawlable /claims.json. Every one of these bets deletes or freezes hundreds of those pages. check-claim-usage.mjs was written because 20 rotted edges had already made the site "publish 20 false statements about where its own claims are cited — inside the very artifact whose job is to prove it does not make things up." CONDITION, binding on all six: no retirement PR merges without same-commit surgery on used_in, and the retirement plan states which claims lose their last citing page and therefore leave the registry.

rulings.subject: CROSS-CUTTING — the fence is a habit, not a gate
rulings.why: check-fabrications.mjs is a blocklist of five named 2026 patterns, not a requirement that numbers be sourced; sourced-claims.json holds 47 claims; check-src-sentinel.mjs does not exist on disk while blog/cost-index-2026-07 carries 45 <!-- src: --> annotations and tells readers at line 852 that those files are "re-checked in CI"; and the rule that every number be registered, cited or labeled lives in a CLAUDE.md that reached 1 of 108 sessions. All six bets increase published-claim volume. CONDITION, binding on all six and correctly sequenced first by five of them: the July post is corrected in place, check-src-sentinel.mjs ships in the same PR, and the line-852 drawer stops describing a gate that does not exist — because a false claim about the company's own machinery, on a public repo, with the refutation recipe printed beside it, is categorically worse for this brand than a stale number.

rulings.subject: CROSS-CUTTING — headcount and scale projection
rulings.why: The one hard line, and every bet respects it. All six name the one-person constraint explicitly, none invents staff, cohorts, users or customers, and each labels its prices as unvalidated hypotheses in its own text — index-is-the-company states "EVERY PRICE ABOVE IS AN UNVALIDATED HYPOTHESIS," open-institution calls $44,880 "the proof-of-mechanism year" and refuses to call it a venture outcome, bookkeeper concedes its ceiling is "a very good one-person business," price-inversion prints its $288K ceiling arithmetic, and radical-narrowing says outright "the labour business does not scale and I am not pretending it does." Projecting capability is allowed and all six do it honestly.

lens: The First-Dollar Critic — tracing the literal shortest path from 2026-08-07 to one dollar received, counting weeks and naming every hidden precondition.
thesis: Every one of these six documents is a company strategy, and only three of them are a revenue plan. The decisive fact none of the six states plainly is that Muntin currently has no mechanism to accept money from anyone, for anything: zero files under `apps/web` call `/v1/billing/checkout/begin` (grep returns 0), `priceIdForTier` has three branches and no per-location or per-client one, `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` is unset, and the checkout success URL points at `/settings/billing` — a directory that does not exist on disk. Worse for every product bet, the storefront cannot deliver a human to the product at all: 516 HTML references point at the unrouted `ledger.muntin.digital` and **zero** point at `app.muntin.digital`, where the product actually lives. So "billing exists for three tiers" is true only at the API layer; commercially the company is one whole surface further from a dollar than any of these plans assumes, and adding a $19 or $600 or $79 SKU changes nothing while there is no buy button and no route to the app. That collapses the field: the only 90-day dollar available is **revenue that never touches the product** — an invoice from a one-person analysis desk over data that stays free, which the methodology page's independence clause (verified at `cost-index/methodology/index.html:514-515`: no submitters, no vendor feed, no sponsorship, no pay-to-be-listed) permits explicitly and which needs no SKU, no route, no launch, and no correctness fix to the food-cost identity. Three bets exploit that loophole (index-is-the-company, radical-narrowing's Lock List, open-institution's attestation) and three ignore it entirely, staking dollar one on a product that has never been run end to end by anyone. Among the three that exploit it, the differentiator is not the mechanism but the outbound motion: `dream-bookkeeper-platform` schedules 20 buyer conversations and `dream-index-is-the-company` schedules 10, while `dream-radical-narrowing` schedules zero and relies on a 777-address list that has never been mailed and whose send path is hard-capped at `CAP = 90` per run on Resend's free tier. The honest shortest path to one dollar is a composite no single document contains — correct the July post, get invoicing capability, then spend Don's 15 discretionary hours on 20-30 conversations with DMV multi-unit groups and restaurant-specialist bookkeeping firms, selling a custom-basket or cost-review engagement at $1,500-5,000 — and it lands at roughly week 8-10, not week 4 and not week 52. Every plan that instead front-loads correctness work, page amputation, or a record layer is spending the quarter on assets that close a sale nobody has yet started.

rulings.subject: dream-index-is-the-company — the Reference Desk, custom baskets, certified feed
rulings.why: CLOSEST TO A DOLLAR, and the only document that says the quiet part correctly: 'the first dollar is an invoice from a one-person company... it needs no product, no billing code and no launch.' That is verified true — the independence clause at methodology:514-515 forecloses only submitters, vendor feeds, sponsorship and pay-to-be-listed, leaving analysis and service entirely sellable. It also schedules the outbound motion (10 conversations, ~6 founder-hours). PATH: week 1-3 correct the July post (you cannot invite verification of a page carrying 72 false claims and a cite drawer promising a CI gate that is not on disk); week 2-8 the 10 calls; week 8-12 first engagement invoiced. WEEKS TO DOLLAR: 8-12. BINDING PRECONDITION: the lead offer must be the CUSTOM BASKET ENGAGEMENT ($2,500-7,500 setup), not the $250-500/mo Desk subscription. The Desk sells interpretation to institutions that already get 'food prices are up' free from BLS/USDA ERS/NRA — the document's own failure section concedes this and concedes every price is an unvalidated hypothesis. A custom basket weighted to one DMV group's actual purchase mix is a concrete deliverable with a named buyer in Don's own network, and it is the honest paid version of the thing the frozen public weights refuse to be. SECOND CONDITION: three of the ten named call targets (two trade-press desks, two culinary programs) cannot buy. Replace them with operators and firms. Also note the plan's Reference Plate, DOI, embeds and press page are all CLOSING assets — they help a skeptic who already arrived, and none of them makes anyone arrive; they must not be allowed to consume the weeks the calls need.

rulings.subject: dream-bookkeeper-platform — sell the firm, restaurants come free
rulings.why: OWNS THE BEST ASSET IN THE ENTIRE SET AND BURIES IT: 20 scheduled outbound conversations with a named, reachable, budget-holding buyer segment. It is also the only bet that correctly removes correctness from the critical path by gating the food-cost identity behind a certification flag and shipping the AP leg (capture -> GL-code -> post -> workpaper) that is already accounting-correct. BUT AS WRITTEN IT SCHEDULES THE WRONG WORK FIRST. A `firms` entity, a client-org edge, firm-billed Stripe, a /cockpit Next.js route, and the billing.ts:175 seat fix are all named as build items — and NONE of them is required for dollar one. A firm can be invoiced. `stripe_subscriptions.org_id` blocks a firm from being a self-serve SaaS tenant; it does not block Don from sending a ten-client firm a $540 invoice for a pilot month. Defer the entire schema rebuild until after a firm has paid once. WEEKS TO DOLLAR IF RESEQUENCED: 8-12 for a paid pilot; the plan's own honest number for a real subscription is JANUARY — it states firms do not change AP tooling mid-engagement and a bet started in August has one switching window and then waits twelve months, which is ~22 weeks, not 90 days. BINDING PRECONDITION: the 15 founder-hours of calls actually happen against 13-26 discretionary hours/month and ~53 hours of standing obligations — this is most of one month's entire budget and nothing else in the plan may compete with it. HIDDEN PREREQUISITE THE PLAN UNDERWEIGHTS: MarginEdge [me] finance has served restaurant accountants since 2023-06-27, so the 'nobody' white space was three years stale when written; the fence (POS-tethered, ~$350/location, does not reach 1-3-location independents on Clover) may not matter to a firm that already has the vendor relationship.

rulings.subject: dream-radical-narrowing — the Lock List at $49/mo
rulings.why: CONTAINS THE SINGLE FASTEST REVENUE INSTRUMENT ON THE BOARD AND THEN CHAINS IT TO THE HEAVIEST DEMOLITION. The paid Lock List is a Stripe payment link over writing the free monthly dispatch already obligates — zero billing code, zero product, zero launch, and it RETIRES an obligation rather than adding one. That is correct and it is the cheapest dollar in the register. WEEKS TO DOLLAR: 6-8, IF de-coupled. BINDING PRECONDITION AND THE REASON THIS IS NOT A PASS: the bet schedules ZERO buyer conversations and routes its entire demand through a mailing list it has never mailed. I verified the send path — `src/worker.js` line ~8793 filters `sub.source !== 'cost-index'` AND carries `const CAP = 90; // Resend free tier is 100/day — stay under; larger lists need batching/queue`. So 'widen the filter, reach 775' is one line PLUS batching PLUS a paid Resend tier, and the first blast to a 15-month-cold list will generate spam complaints on the same sending domain that serves magic-link auth. Budget a warming ramp. SECOND CONDITION: the plan's own modal failure — 'the cut half-lands and the company ends up strictly worse' — is real, and ~15 agent sessions plus ~20 founder-hours of irreversible deletion of 1,100 routes, all Spanish prose, and the entire count feature is NOT on the path to the $49. Take the payment link and the mailable list; fund the amputation separately or not at all. THIRD: the product being sold ('37 of 100 are priceable this month') is a claim about Muntin's own confidence, which the document itself flags may be honest and unwanted, and the free dispatch already gives away the same writing — the paid tier's differentiation is thin and should be tested at $49 before anyone believes it.

rulings.subject: dream-price-inversion — $600/location signed monthly close
rulings.why: THE BEST ECONOMIC DIAGNOSIS IN THE SET AND NO CUSTOMER-ACQUISITION MOTION AT ALL. It is correct that $19 forecloses every human-touch channel at a $450-600 lifetime value, correct that a per-location quantity sidesteps the billing.ts:174-175 seat multiplication rather than patching it, correct that independents demonstrably pay $350-500 for a measured food-cost number, and correct that annual billing must not land the first charge in mid-February. But trace the path: seven named correctness fixes (Purchases leg re-derivation, location predicate, count tail fill, footing legs, dollar coverage, withhold rules, two label corrections) -> one real month on Tacombi -> specimen close published -> CPA validation -> post price -> applications arrive -> convert -> bill. COUNT THE PRECONDITIONS: a location-attribution product decision only the founder can make; a CPA saying yes to the market prior under ASC 330 (the plan concedes a no collapses the short-count premise entirely); the first end-to-end product run in company history; a $600 per-location Stripe SKU that does not exist; a checkout surface that does not exist anywhere in apps/web; and a route from storefront to app that does not exist — 516 dead `ledger.muntin.digital` refs, zero to `app.muntin.digital`. THE FATAL OMISSION: the whole thesis is 'at $600 the founder can afford to talk to the check-signer himself,' and the plan then schedules exactly TWO conversations — one CPA and one bookkeeper, neither of whom is the buyer. It expects ~10 qualified applicants to find `/close/apply/` on a site with 4 waitlist forms and no measured traffic. WEEKS TO DOLLAR: 20-30 realistically, gated on a product nobody has run once. The price thesis should be salvaged into whichever bet wins; the plan as sequenced is another quarter of building for nobody, which is precisely the failure it names in its own fourth paragraph.

rulings.subject: dream-open-institution — attestation at $250 per certified as-of statement
rulings.why: THE MOST HONEST DOCUMENT IN THE SET, AND ITS HONESTY IS THE VERDICT. The attestation mechanism is genuinely elegant: CC0 lets anyone reference a reading for free but does not let anyone PROVE what the reading was on a date, the 10,294-entry revisions ledger is exactly why that proof would have value, the frozen editions spine already exists, the payer is a relyer and never a subject, and the first certificate can be produced by hand from artifacts on disk today. Zero infrastructure. But the document itself writes the refutation: 'it rests on a single unevidenced premise: that somewhere there exists a person about to sign a document who wants to name a neutral, dated food-price reference in it. I have no artifact supporting that. Zero people have asked Muntin for anything in roughly fifteen months.' The dependency is circular and total — attestation value is a function of index adoption, and index adoption is zero. Nobody escalates a produce contract against a reference no counterparty has heard of. WEEKS TO DOLLAR: unbounded; the plan's own day-90 tripwire falls back to $390/yr membership, which BUNDLES LEDGER and therefore re-inherits every product precondition this bet was designed to escape. The 20 scheduled founder conversations are the right instinct and should be lifted out. The record layer (corrections, calibration, refusals, freshness) is real and worth building — but the document correctly names it a CLOSING asset, and a closing asset cannot produce a first dollar when no sale has been opened.

rulings.subject: dream-vindication-instrument — the free Market Sheet, Ledger at $79/location/month
rulings.why: IT ADMITS IN ITS OWN 90-DAY LIST THAT IT PRODUCES NO DOLLAR: 'Post the price and the arithmetic: $79/location/month... Mark it honestly as not yet billable.' All revenue is product revenue, and the product cannot be bought — no $79 SKU, no fourth priceIdForTier branch, no checkout surface in apps/web, no /settings/billing route for the success URL to land on, and no storefront link to app.muntin.digital. The acquisition mechanic (operator prints sheet -> vendor rep sees paper in a room -> rep types the URL off the footer) propagates, in the document's own words, 'at the speed of a sales route, not a launch,' and its primary failure mode is that the rep's rehearsed first sentence — 'that's terminal market, not your landed cost' — is TRUE and already documented in the company's own IS-IT-YOU-OR-THE-MARKET.md as the thing that loses the argument. WEEKS TO DOLLAR: longest in the set. BUT LIFT ONE MOVE INTO WHATEVER WINS: 'Don prints one sheet and takes it to one rep, then a second the following week, and writes down verbatim what the rep says first.' Two founder-hours, week 3, zero dollars, and it tests the operator-demand premise that four of the other five bets silently assume. It is the cheapest falsification experiment anywhere in the register and it should be run regardless of which strategy is chosen. Also worth salvaging: 42 of 132 modules in tools/_shared — pack-shrink, vendor-switch, silent-bleed — are fully written, parity-locked, honesty-gated and referenced by zero HTML pages.

rulings.subject: CROSS-CUTTING: the storefront cannot deliver a single visitor to the product
rulings.why: Verified this session and named by NONE of the six documents: HTML across the storefront carries 28,349 references to `https://muntin.digital` and 516 to `https://ledger.muntin.digital` — a host neither repo routes and which appears nowhere in wrangler.jsonc — and exactly ZERO references to `app.muntin.digital`, where apps/web actually deploys. The live product is unreachable from the marketing site by any link. Every bet whose dollar rides on the product (price-inversion, vindication, bookkeeper-platform's subscription, open-institution's membership) inherits this silently. dream-vindication proposes repointing 410 of those CTAs — but to `/market-sheet/`, not to the product. This is roughly one agent session to fix and it is an absolute precondition for any product revenue; the fact that fifteen months produced 516 dead product CTAs and zero live ones is the single clearest measurement of how far this company is from selling anything.

rulings.subject: CROSS-CUTTING: there is no buy button anywhere in the company
rulings.why: `grep -rn 'checkout/begin' apps/web` returns 0. `priceIdForTier` has exactly three branches (solo/team/accountant) reading STRIPE_PRICE_SOLO/TEAM/ACCOUNTANT_BASE. `stripeKey` returns null with STRIPE_SECRET_KEY unset, so stripePost fails closed. And `BILLING_CHECKOUT_SUCCESS_URL` defaults to `/settings/billing?status=ok` — I listed apps/web/app/(product)/settings/ and there is no `billing` directory, so even a successful Stripe redirect lands on a 404. The verified fact 'billing exists for three tiers' is therefore true only at the API layer. Any bet costing its billing work as 'add a fourth SKU' is understating by an entire web surface plus a live Stripe account plus an env rotation. CONSEQUENCE FOR SEQUENCING: the first dollar must be INVOICED, not charged. An invoice needs no code and can be sent this month; a checkout flow is a Q4 project that produces revenue only if a buyer already exists — which is exactly the thing not yet established.

rulings.subject: CROSS-CUTTING: the 775-subscriber unlock is not a one-line fix
rulings.why: Four of six bets treat widening the `sub.source` filter at src/worker.js:8793 as the largest cheap distribution act available. The filter fix is real and is one line. What sits four lines above it is not mentioned by any of them: `const CAP = 90;   // Resend free tier is 100/day — stay under; larger lists need batching/queue`. Reaching 777 addresses needs batching or a queue plus a paid Resend tier. Compounding it: this list has been collecting for ~15 months and has never received a single message, so a cold blast will draw spam complaints against a sending domain shared with magic-link auth (`RESEND_API_KEY`, `MAGIC_LINK_BASE_URL`) — a deliverability incident there breaks sign-in, not just marketing. CONDITION: widen the filter, but warm the list in tranches under 90 and lead with the July correction, which is both the strongest possible first contact and the only defensible one given 72 live falsehoods on the flagship.

rulings.subject: CROSS-CUTTING: revenue that requires no product is the only 90-day dollar, and only three bets reach for it
rulings.why: Verified at cost-index/methodology/index.html:514-515 — 'No market participant submits a price to us' and 'No vendor feed, no sponsorship, no pay-to-be-listed.' Nothing in the independence contract forecloses interpretation, custom analysis, service, support or expertise sold over data that stays free. That loophole is real, it is large, and it dissolves FOUR blockers simultaneously: the missing SKU, the missing checkout surface, the `stripe_subscriptions.org_id` schema block on firms, and the entire Purchases-leg correctness debt. dream-index-is-the-company exploits it explicitly and best; dream-radical-narrowing exploits it at $49/mo; dream-open-institution exploits it into a buyer with no evidence. dream-price-inversion and dream-vindication ignore it entirely and stake everything on a product that has never run once. THE HONEST SHORTEST PATH, which belongs to no single document: (wk 1-3) correct the July post and stand up invoicing; (wk 2-8) Don spends ~15 hours on 20-30 conversations with DMV multi-unit groups and restaurant-specialist bookkeeping firms; (wk 8-10) first custom-basket or cost-review engagement invoiced at $1,500-5,000. That is the composite of index-is-the-company's mechanism and bookkeeper-platform's outbound motion, and it is the only sequence in the register that ends in money this quarter.

rulings.subject: CROSS-CUTTING: no bet schedules enough buyer conversations, and the one irreplaceable input is founder-hours
rulings.why: Scheduled buyer-facing conversations by bet: bookkeeper-platform 20, open-institution 20, index-is-the-company 10 (of which 4 targets cannot buy), price-inversion 2 (neither is a buyer), vindication 2 (reps, not buyers), radical-narrowing 0. Against ~13-26 discretionary founder-hours/month and ~53 hours of standing obligations, 20 calls at 45 minutes is ~15 hours — most of one entire month's budget. Every plan also asks for 6+ founder-hours to run the product end to end, 1-2 hours for a credential decision on FRED/BLS/AMS keys, and 20-30 minutes of irreversible naming and pricing calls. These compete directly. CONDITION FOR ANY PLAN TO BE CREDIBLE: it must state explicitly what the founder does NOT do during the quarter the calls happen. None of the six does. The correct posture is that agent sessions are effectively unlimited and founder-hours are the only scarce input, so every founder-hour spent on anything other than a conversation with a potential buyer, the one end-to-end product run, and the credential decision is an hour that does not produce a first customer.
